title: On-call & Incident Response: Standards and Templates
author: Priya Patel
body:
Overview:
This document defines Redwood Inference's standard incident lifecycle, severity definitions, runbook templates, postmortem process, on-call rotation guidelines, game day plans, and status page / customer communication templates. It is intended for engineers, SREs, product managers, and support staff who participate in incident management and post-incident operations.

Scope:
- Applies to all production service incidents across Redwood-hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments where Redwood has responsibility for runtime, control plane, or customer-facing API behavior.
- Includes steps for detection, triage, mitigation, communication, post-incident review, and follow-up.

1) Incident severity definitions (quick reference):
- P0 (SEV0) \u2014 Service Down / Data Loss
  - Impact: Major customer-facing outage or systemic data loss/corruption impacting >50% of customers or critical path functionality (request failures, persistent 500s, control plane unavailability).
  - Target response: ACK within 5 minutes, mitigation plan within 15 minutes.
- P1 (SEV1) \u2014 Degraded Critical Functionality
  - Impact: Significant degradation or performance regression impacting a large subset of customers (>10%) or key SLA violations (latency, errors).
  - Target response: ACK within 15 minutes, mitigation plan within 30 minutes.
- P2 (SEV2) \u2014 Partial Degradation / Single-customer impact
  - Impact: Isolated failures, partial feature degradation, or throttling that affects limited customers.
  - Target response: ACK within 1 business hour, mitigation plan within 4 hours.
- P3 (SEV3) \u2014 Minor issues / cosmetic
  - Impact: Non-critical bugs, UI inconsistencies, docs, or low-severity alerts.
  - Target response: Triage in next sprint or within 3 business days.

2) Incident lifecycle (step-by-step):
1. Detection & Alerting
   - Monitoring systems (Prometheus/Alertmanager, Datadog, internal telemetry) generate alerts.
   - PagerDuty triggers on-call depending on severity & routing rules.
   - First responder ACKs alert in PagerDuty and joins incident channel (Slack #inc-<service>-<id> or dedicated incident bridge).
2. Triage & Severity Assessment
   - First responder posts initial diagnosis: symptoms, scope, estimated impact, and suggested severity.
   - If uncertain, escalate to SRE lead or service owner within 15 minutes for P0/P1.
3. Mitigation & Short-term Fixes
   - Apply runbook playbooks or safe mitigation (rollback, scale-up, circuit-breaker) with a single responsible actor.
   - For P0/P1, assign an incident commander (IC) within 15 minutes who runs prioritized checklist.
4. Communication
   - Internal: IC updates Slack incident channel with impact, mitigation steps, and ETA every 15 minutes for P0/P1 and every 60 minutes for P2.
   - External: Status page update and customer comms (see templates). Customer Success drafts targeted messages for affected customers.
5. Recovery & Validation
   - Validate metrics (error rates, p99 latency, successful request rate) before declaring recovery.
   - IC declares "Service Degraded" or "Service Restored" status on status page and closes escalation once validated.
6. Postmortem & Follow-up
   - Owner (usually service/product) files postmortem within 72 hours of incident resolution.
   - Create follow-up tasks in tracker (Jira) with owners and target completion dates.
   - Track remediation in a follow-up registry until verified.

3) Roles & responsibilities:
- Incident Commander (IC): Coordinates run, communications, triage decisions, escalation, and post-incident actions. Assigned for P0/P1 incidents.
- Primary on-call / First Responder: ACKs pager, performs initial triage, executes first-step mitigations, and escalates to IC if needed.
- Service Owner: Provides domain expertise, approves rollbacks/rollouts and postmortem author.
- SRE Lead: Handles cross-service escalations, capacity, and infrastructure-level mitigations.
- Customer Success / Support: Manages customer communications and triage for impacted customers.
- Engineering Manager: Oversees resourcing for follow-up remediation.

4) Runbook template (use per-service; kept in service repo and referenced here):
- Title: <service-name> production P0 runbook
- Pager & Playbook: Commands to run, dashboards to view, logs to tail
  - Quick checks: 
    1) Check API gateway error rate: queries per minute, 5xx count
    2) Check model-serving fleet health: GPU host count, free memory, OOM events
    3) Check queue/backpressure metrics: request queue length, token backlog
  - Common mitigations (ordered):
    a) Scale up replicas (kubectl/terraform autoscale)
    b) Disable non-critical routes/features (feature flag)
    c) Bounce component (graceful restart)
    d) Rollback last deployment (k8s rolling rollback)
  - Safety & approvals: list commands requiring approval and approver contact
- Validation checklist: metrics to confirm service is healthy (error rate <0.5%, p99 latency < target)
- Post-incident steps: logs to capture, artifacts to attach to postmortem

Example runbook table (configuration):
| Item | Command / Location | Owner |
|------|--------------------|-------|
| Check API errors | Datadog dashboard: api.production.errors | oncall |
| Scale model pool | ops/k8s/scale.sh --service <svc> --replicas N | oncall/SRE |
| Rollback deployment | kubectl rollout undo deployment/<svc> -n prod | service-owner |

5) Escalation matrix (example):
- First responder -> service owner (5-15 minutes for P0/P1)
- Service owner -> SRE lead (15-30 minutes)
- SRE lead -> Eng Director / CTO (30-60 minutes for ongoing P0)
- For cross-tenant data-loss incidents, notify Legal and Security within 60 minutes.

6) On-call rotations & expectations:
- Rotation cadence: 1 week primary on-call per engineer, 2-week secondary/backfill (team decides).
- Handoff: Each shift must publish a Handoff note in Slack #oncall-handoffs with active issues, maintenance windows, and any escalations.
- Coverage: At least two people should be able to own each critical service.
- Time-off & swaps: Use the on-call calendar (GCal) and update PagerDuty. Swaps require coverage confirmation from replacement.
- Training: New on-call engineers must shadow two rotations and complete the service runbook checklist before taking primary.

7) Game days (planned exercises):
Purpose: Validate runbooks, SLOs, telemetry, and team coordination.
- Frequency: Quarterly per platform domain (serving, control plane, infra).
- Scenario design: Representative P0 and multi-service cascade scenarios. Include partial hardware failures (GPU host loss), model OOM, and region outage.
- Roles during game day: IC, Scribe, Observability lead, Customer Comms, Service Owners.
- Success criteria: Mean time to mitigate (MTTM) improvement, runbook coverage, and automated rollback verified.
- Artifacts: Game day report with metrics, timeline, and action items uploaded to the incident registry.

8) Postmortem process & template (mandatory for P0/P1; recommended for P2):
- Timeline: Postmortem draft within 72 hours, review within 7 days, public (internal) publish within 10 days.
- Objective: Describe timeline, root cause(s), impact, mitigation steps, action items with owners and due dates, and preventative measures.
- Blamelessness: We follow a blameless culture; focus on system fixes and process gaps.

Postmortem template (plain):
- Title: YYYY-MM-DD \u2014 <service> \u2014 <brief description>
- Summary: 2-3 sentence overview of incident and impact
- Impact: Affected customers, duration, metrics (error %, requests affected)
- Timeline: Ordered bullet list with timestamps (UTC) and responsible actor for each event
- Root cause: Technical and organizational contributing factors
- Immediate remediation: Steps taken to stop/mitigate incident
- Long-term fixes: Action items (Jira entries) with owner and ETA
- Follow-up validation: How we will verify the fix and when
- Lessons learned & runbook updates required

9) Status page & customer communications (templates):
- Status page guidance:
  - Status page should contain clear status: Operational / Degraded / Partial Outage / Major Outage / Maintenance
  - Update cadence: initial update within 30 minutes for P0/P1, follow-up every 30-60 minutes until resolved.
  - Include: What\u2019s affected, who\u2019s impacted, what we\u2019re doing, ETA for next update.

- External customer template \u2014 initial notice (short):
"To our customers,

We are currently investigating elevated error rates affecting the Redwood API in the <region>. Some requests are failing with 5xx errors. Our engineering team has been paged and is actively investigating. We will provide an update within 30 minutes. If you are experiencing critical customer impact, please contact support@redwood.ai with your request ID and severity.

\u2014 Redwood Inference Operations"

- External customer template \u2014 follow-up & resolution (short):
"Update: The issue affecting the Redwood API in <region> has been resolved as of <time UTC>. Root cause: <short cause>. Impact: <summary of affected customers/requests>. Remediation: <steps taken>. Next steps: <planned follow-ups and expected timeline>. If you continue to see errors, please contact support@redwood.ai.

\u2014 Redwood Inference Operations"

- Customer success targeted template (for impacted customers):
"Hi <Customer Name>,

We detected an incident impacting <feature/service>. Our team mitigated the issue at <time UTC>. We estimate that <percent> of requests were affected between <start> and <end>. We are following up with a detailed postmortem and remediation plan. Please let us know if you need additional information or assistance.

Sincerely,
Redwood Customer Success"

10) Metrics & SLOs to monitor during incidents:
- Error rate (5xx) by endpoint and model variant (target: <0.5% for normal operations)
- Request success rate and QPS by region
- P99 and P95 latency per route and per model (SLO thresholds defined in service SLO doc)
- Model-serving node health: GPU memory pressure, OOM events, queue length
- Autoscaler events and throttles

11) Incident artifacts & evidence checklist (what to capture before closing):
- Incident timeline (Slack thread and PagerDuty timestamps)
- Key logs and traces (traced requests with IDs)
- Dashboards/screenshots used for triage (Datadog links)
- List of commands run and config changes (git commit ids, k8s manifests)
- Postmortem link and linked Jira remediation tasks

12) Ownership & contact list:
- On-call rotations: team-specific calendar (link to team calendar) and PagerDuty schedules
- Incident exec contact: Eng Director (on-call escalation) \u2014 eng-director@redwood.ai
- Security & Legal escalation: security-escalations@redwood.ai, legal@redwood.ai

13) Change history & governance:
- This doc is reviewed quarterly by Eng SRE and Runtime teams. Significant process changes require approval from the SRE lead and Head of Engineering.

Appendices:
A) Quick CLI play snippets (examples):
- Tail app logs: kubectl logs -f deployment/<svc> -n prod --since=30m | grep ERROR
- Scale replicas: ./ops/k8s/scale.sh --service <svc> --replicas 8
- Rollback: kubectl rollout undo deployment/<svc> -n prod

B) Example incident timeline excerpt (format):
- 2026-02-12T14:03Z \u2014 PagerDuty alert triggered (5xx spike) \u2014 first responder ACK
- 2026-02-12T14:07Z \u2014 Service owner engaged; initial mitigation: scale model pool + disable experimental route
- 2026-02-12T14:28Z \u2014 Error rate reduced to baseline; IC declares degraded -> monitoring

C) Where to store runbooks and postmortems:
- Canonical runbooks: service repo under /docs/runbooks/production.md and referenced in Confluence service index.
- Postmortems: Confluence under /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/postmortems/YYYY/ and linked in Jira tickets.

Contact & feedback:
If you have suggestions to improve this document or templates, open an RFC in the eng-docs repo or contact the SRE lead.
